metadata.title: Ember & Oak
metadata.description: Ember & Oak is a wood-fired restaurant serving seasonal, ingredient-driven cooking.

footer.tagline: Seasonal, wood-fired cooking in the heart of the city.

hero.subtitle: The finest ingredients. Live-fire cooking. Extraordinary service.

about.title: Our story
about.intro: Ember & Oak opened with a simple idea: cook good ingredients over real fire, and let them speak for themselves.

woodFired.label: Wood-fired
woodFired.description: Every dish passes near the hearth at some point.

seasonal.label: Seasonal
seasonal.description: Menu changes with what local farms bring us.

familyRun.label: Family run
familyRun.description: Owned and run by the same family since day one.

established.label: Est. 2015
established.description: A decade in the neighborhood, and counting.

fire.title: Cooking over real flame
fire.body: Our kitchen is built around a wood-burning hearth, not a line of gas burners. It's slower, it's less forgiving, and it's the whole point — real fire gives food a depth you can't fake. Nearly everything that leaves the kitchen, from the bread to the dessert, passes near the flame at some point.

ingredients.title: Seasonal, sourced close to home
ingredients.body: We work with local farms, fishmongers, and butchers to build a menu that actually changes with the seasons — not a laminated menu that never moves. If a vegetable isn't good this week, it isn't on the plate this week. That's the deal we've made with our suppliers, and with our guests.

table.title: Hospitality first
table.body: It's a small dining room with a big focus on hospitality. We want every table to feel like a regular's table, whether it's your first visit or your fiftieth. Servers who know the menu inside out, a room that isn't trying too hard, and food that gets to you hot.

about.quote: “Whether you’re joining us for a quiet weeknight dinner or a celebration, we’re glad you’re here.”

notes.diningRoom: Worn leather, low light, and tables close enough to hear the kitchen work.
notes.hearth: Oak and applewood, stacked and burning since 4pm. Every plate passes near it once.
notes.ribeye: 14 ounces, charred hard on the outside, pink all the way through the middle.
notes.bar: House cocktails and a red blend that changes with whatever the sommelier opened last.
notes.privateEvents: Long tables, no minimum-spend lecture — just tell us how many and when.
notes.dessert: Whatever's ripe gets torched, curded, or given a crust.
